newsitem.title: VIETNAM: APEC meeting not obsessed with currencies - Rubin.
newsitem.headline: APEC meeting not obsessed with currencies - Rubin.

text.p: Asia Pacific nations were not preoccupied with currencies at their weekend meeting, but instead concentrated on practical steps they could take to improve the functioning of their financial markets, U.S. Treasury Secretary Robert Rubin said on Sunday.

"They weren't obsessed with exchange rates. There was almost no discussion of that," Rubin told reporters on his way here from the meeting in the Philippines of finance ministers from the Asia Pacific Economic Cooperation (APEC) group.
He described the mood of the meeting as realistic.
A few years ago, some of the countries were riding high on the back of big inflows of foreign capital into their markets. But that has now changed.
"Some of them are having some problems," Rubin said. "Korea is having some problems. Thailand is having some problems. I think that created a sense of realism."
The Treasury chief though pronounced himself pleased with the results of the meeting, which set out a specific plan of action to improve the workings of the region's financial markets.
"This really has been a very valuable meeting," Rubin said.

APEC is comprised of Australia, Brunei, Canada, Chile, China, Hong Kong, Indonesia, Japan, Malaysia, Mexico, New Zealand, Papua New Guinea, the Philippines, Singapore, South Korea, Taiwan, Thailand and the United States.
